vendor_and_service: Resort PMS vendor (SYS-01, with card vault)
tier_rationale: About 410,000 guest profiles and 152,000 ID scans; virtual card vault; supports High processes BP-01, BP-03, BP-04; will host the managed hotels from 2027
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2 plus bridge letter; annual service provider AOC; responsibility matrix
pci_dss_aoc: Service provider AOC dated 2026-02, covering the card vault and payment interfaces
subservice_organizations: Public cloud hosting provider carved out
exceptions_noted: 1 exception: 2 of 25 vendor staff leavers removed after the 1-day target; remediated per management response
cuecs_and_company_mapping: User provisioning and removal; least-privilege roles including the card display permission; SSO with MFA; review of user activity reports; protection of workstations used to reach SYS-01. Mapped to AC-2, AC-6, IA-2(1), AU-6, SI-3. Company gaps: POAM-001, POAM-002, POAM-005, POAM-014
availability_vs_bia: Stated RTO 4 h and RPO 15 min: meets BP-03 and BP-04 (RTO 4 h, RPO 1 h) but **not BP-01** (RTO 2 h). Not in the contract (P05 finding 1)
incident_notification_terms: Notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident (system description); contract silent
follow_up: Contract amendment: RTO and RPO, notice within 24 hours of suspecting a card data incident and no later than 10 days for personal information (Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a)); ask the vendor to add Confidentiality, which the REIT requires; obtain the hosting provider's report summary

vendor_and_service: Managed security service provider (MSSP; operates SYS-12 SIEM)
tier_rationale: Privileged EDR agents on 470 PCs; security logs; supports detection for every process
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2 (Security) plus bridge letter; annual service review with detection tests
pci_dss_aoc: Not applicable (no card data in scope of its service)
exceptions_noted: 1 exception: high-severity escalation missed the 30-minute target in 1 of 40 samples; staffing added
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer defines log sources, maintains the escalation list, approves containment, and reviews monthly reports. Mapped to AU-2, SI-4, IR-4. Company gaps: missing log sources (POAM-005, POAM-014)
availability_vs_bia: Not a recovery provider; its own continuity plan was tested in the period
incident_notification_terms: Contract: call within 30 minutes on high severity
follow_up: Obtain the SIEM platform provider's SOC 2 summary; add Availability to the next report request; track the escalation target monthly

tier_rationale: Authentication for every company system including SYS-01; supports all processes
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2 plus status history review
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer configures MFA, conditional access, administrator roles, and break-glass accounts. Mapped to IA-2(1), AC-2, AC-6. Company gap: phishing-resistant MFA for administrators (POAM-004)
availability_vs_bia: 99.99% monthly uptime commitment; no RTO stated
incident_notification_terms: Security incident notice per terms of service

vendor_and_service: Public cloud provider (SYS-10 landing zone: data warehouse, CRM, recordings, websites, backups)
tier_rationale: Guest data at scale (warehouse and CRM); call recordings with card data today; backups for all company-managed workloads
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2 and service provider AOC from the provider's compliance portal; shared responsibility review (P04)
pci_dss_aoc: Service provider AOC covering the infrastructure services the company uses (2026)
subservice_organizations: None relevant (provider-operated data centers in scope)
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer is responsible for identity, network rules, encryption keys, logging, and backups inside its accounts (P04 control map). Company gaps: restore tests (POAM-011); recordings with card data (POAM-013)
availability_vs_bia: Multi-zone services and the second-region backup vault meet BP-11, BP-12, and BP-15; the warehouse and CRM restore times are untested
incident_notification_terms: Per service terms; the company's monitoring detects most account-level events first
bridge_letter: Not needed (report period plus provider status history)
follow_up: Keep the provider's shared responsibility model mapped in P04; re-download reports each year

vendor_and_service: Booking engine vendor (SYS-05, payment form embedded by iframe)
tier_rationale: Card data for about 35,000 prepayments a year; supports BP-04
assurance_required: Annual service provider AOC; SOC 2 Type 2
report_type_and_period: SOC 2 Type 1 as of 2025-12-31 (no Type 2 yet)
cuecs_and_company_mapping: The vendor secures the payment form; the company is responsible for the scripts on its own pages that embed it (PCI DSS 6.4.3 and 11.6.1). Company gap: POAM-015
availability_vs_bia: Vendor states 99.9% uptime; downtime is covered by CRO and channel bookings (BP-04 RTO 4 h)
incident_notification_terms: Notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident
follow_up: Require a Type 2 report at the 2027 renewal; written PCI DSS responsibility matrix (POAM-012)

vendor_and_service: Channel manager (SYS-05; online travel agency connectivity and virtual cards)
tier_rationale: Virtual card numbers for about 30,000 bookings a year pass through it; supports BP-04
assurance_required: Annual service provider AOC; SOC 2 Type 2 if available
pci_dss_aoc: Service provider AOC dated 2025-04: **expired** for annual purposes (PCI DSS 12.8.4)
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Company controls: API credentials and user access to the channel manager portal. Mapped to IA-5, AC-2
availability_vs_bia: No commitment stated; outage stops online travel agency inventory updates (overbooking risk, BP-04 RPO 1 h)
follow_up: Current AOC by 2027-01-31 or begin replacement; add notice and recovery terms (POAM-012; P01 R-021)

vendor_and_service: Contact center platform vendor (SYS-15; CRO calls, recording capture, AI transcription)
tier_rationale: Carries spoken card numbers and security codes in calls; recordings land in the company's cloud account; supports BP-05
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2; service provider AOC because card data passes through its platform
pci_dss_aoc: **None.** The vendor says card data is out of its scope because recordings are stored by the customer; voice card data still passes through its platform
subservice_organizations: Cloud hosting and the speech-to-text model provider carved out
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer controls recording settings, retention, user access, and where recordings are stored. Company gaps: recordings with card data (POAM-013); call recording notice (P10 AI-003)
availability_vs_bia: Stated RTO 8 h; BP-05 needs RTO 4 h. Workaround: route CRO calls to the resort front desks
incident_notification_terms: Notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident
follow_up: Pause-and-resume recording and keypad entry remove card data from calls (POAM-013, POAM-016); until then request an AOC or a written PCI DSS responsibility statement; recovery terms at renewal
reviewer_and_date: Security Manager and Director of Central Reservations, 2026-09-01

tier_rationale: Aggregated stay data only (guest names being removed from the extract); supports BP-11 (Low); no card data or privileged access
assurance_required: Security questionnaire and SOC 2 if available, every 2 years; contract terms
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer controls user access and SSO. Company gap: local vendor accounts without SSO (P10)
availability_vs_bia: BP-11 tolerates 72 hours of manual rates
follow_up: Opt out of pooled benchmarking and remove guest names from the extract (P10 AI-001 conditions); ask for a Type 2 report because the service will support the REIT hotels
reviewer_and_date: Director of Revenue Management and GRC Analyst, 2026-09-02

tier_rationale: Guest contact details and questions at scale (about 9,000 conversations a month); 61 transcripts found with card numbers
assurance_required: Annual SOC 2 Type 2; contract terms on retention, masking, and model training
pci_dss_aoc: None. Card numbers should never reach the chatbot; masking is required instead
cuecs_and_company_mapping: Customer configures data retention, masking, and staff access to transcripts. Company gaps: no retention or masking terms (POAM-012, POAM-019)
availability_vs_bia: Not needed for recovery (BP-12 tolerates 8 hours; website and phones remain)
incident_notification_terms: Notice within 5 business days of confirming an incident
follow_up: Contract amendment: 90-day retention, card number masking, no training on company data, notice within 72 hours (P10)
reviewer_and_date: Vice President of Sales and Marketing and Security Manager, 2026-09-02

vendor_and_service: Resort 1 cloud POS and P2PE solution provider (SYS-04)
tier_rationale: Card data for Resort 1 outlets (64 P2PE devices); supports BP-06
assurance_required: Annual P2PE listing check and service provider AOC; SOC 2 Type 2
pci_dss_aoc: Service provider AOC dated 2026-03; solution listed as a validated P2PE solution on the PCI SSC website (checked 2026-08-28)
cuecs_and_company_mapping: The P2PE Instruction Manual requires the merchant to keep a device inventory, inspect devices, and report tampering. Company gaps: device list and inspection logs (POAM-007)
availability_vs_bia: Offline mode stores encrypted transactions for later forwarding; supports BP-06 RTO 4 h
incident_notification_terms: Notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident
follow_up: Keep device inventory and inspection evidence as the PIM requires
reviewer_and_date: Resort Directors of Food and Beverage and GRC Analyst, 2026-08-28

vendor_and_service: Resort 2 legacy POS vendor (SYS-04; support and remote access)
tier_rationale: Always-on remote access into the Resort 2 cardholder data environment; supports BP-06
assurance_required: Annual service provider AOC, or its access assessed within the company's own PCI DSS assessment; contract terms
cuecs_and_company_mapping: The company must control the vendor's access (broker, MFA, session approval) and changes (tickets). Company gaps: POAM-004, POAM-006, POAM-010
availability_vs_bia: Server failure stops outlet card acceptance; no tested fallback (P05 finding 4)
follow_up: Vendor access through the broker by 2026-11-30; include the vendor's access in the 2026 SAQ D scope; contract ends when the P2PE cloud POS replaces the system (2027-06-30)
